records.name: South Philly Food Co-op
records.summary: A community-owned grocery on South Juniper Street in South Philadelphia. Neighbors who become members own a share of the store, and anyone can shop there.
records.what_you_do: Help at community events by tabling, planning events, doing marketing or communications, handling handy jobs such as building displays, phone banking, or office support.

schedule.text: The events page lists the co-op's community events, but its calendar did not load when we checked, so no dates are listed here.

cost.text: Anyone can shop without joining. Member-owners buy a $300 per household equity share, paid in full or in monthly installments over 2 to 12 months. The Community Equity Fund helps people who cannot pay the $300 at once.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the co-op's website, pick the roles you like, and choose whether to get email or text updates.
first_step.basis: Open to the public: anyone can shop, and the volunteer form is public, though the site does not describe a volunteer orientation.
first_step.what_to_expect: Shopping needs no membership, so you can stop in at the store on South Juniper Street. The volunteer form asks for your name, email and an optional phone number, and the site does not say what a first shift looks like.
first_visit_tips: Email the address listed on the volunteer page with questions about a first shift.

records.notes: The /join and /member-ownership pages returned HTTP 403, so the share price comes from the why-become-member-owner page. The volunteer page does not say whether membership is needed to volunteer, so the cost text does not claim it either way. Tier 1 last_sign_of_life (2026-10) is carried over; no newer dated evidence turned up in this pass.

records.name: South Philly Sigma Sharks
records.summary: A youth sports club with girls flag football, tackle football, cheerleading and basketball. Registration for fall 2026 football is open.
records.what_you_do: Kids sign up for a team through the registration forms linked on the site. Adults can volunteer through the site's volunteer page.

schedule.text: Fall football season, with practice sites set by each team's coach. The site lists eight practice sites and two home game sites, but no season start or end dates.

locations.label: Smith Playground (practice site and home games)
James Finnegan Playground (practice site and home games)

cost.text: The site does not list fee amounts. After registering, families pay through Cash App as the site describes, then email the club the child's details and receive a reply with any balance left.

first_step.how: Fill in the football or girls flag football registration form linked from the club's Register page, then pay as the page describes.
first_step.basis: Registration is open to the public through linked forms, and the FAQ and volunteer pages are public, but the site does not describe tryouts or a first practice.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a first practice or tryouts. Each team's coach tells families which of the listed South Philadelphia rec centers and playgrounds the team uses.
first_visit_tips: Ask the coach which practice site your team uses, since the sites vary by team.
Read the refund rules on the FAQ page before you pay, because refunds are limited to a few cases.

records.notes: Age ranges by program from the homepage: girls flag football 9 to 14, tackle football 8 to 13 (birthdate cutoff July 31), cheerleading 6 to 14, basketball with no ages given. The site has no fee amounts, tryout details or season dates. Cheerleading has no tag of its own in our vocabulary, so the closest sports tags are used. The volunteer page takes any role through a Google form and does not mention background checks.

records.name: Southeast Youth Athletic Association (SEYAA)
records.summary: A volunteer-run youth sports league in South Philadelphia. More than 1,000 kids play baseball, soccer and flag football on its five fields at Seventh and Bigler, all year round.
records.what_you_do: Kids join a baseball, soccer or flag football program. Volunteers run the leagues and prepare the fields, and the leagues raise money to cover utilities, insurance and liability costs.

schedule.text: Baseball, soccer and flag football are played year round on the league's fields. Volunteers get the fields ready for summer soccer.

locations.label: League fields
locations.address: Seventh and Bigler streets, South Philadelphia

first_step.how: Ask a volunteer at the league fields at Seventh and Bigler how to sign a child up for baseball, soccer or flag football.
first_step.basis: Open to area kids, but none of the sources we could read publish the sign-up steps, dates or fees.
first_step.what_to_expect: The league plays on five ball fields at Seventh and Bigler, in the shadow of Citizens Bank Park, and volunteers run the leagues. The sources we read do not describe sign-up steps, fees or what a first practice is like.

records.notes: No SEYAA website could be found. Tier 1 listed the website as the bare word SEYAA, which is not an address, so it was removed. A search and a fetch of the guessed address www.seyaa.org (no such site) found no sign-up page. The Inquirer article of May 30, 2026 names Joann McAfee as the volunteer league administrator; the IRS-based contact, Joseph Guercio, is kept as tier 1 had it, so the two names should be checked. The same article mentions a separate complex used by the Delaware Valley Association League. Newcomer rating stays at 2 until a sign-up page or contact is confirmed.

records.name: Southwark/Queen Village Community Garden
records.summary: A food-producing community garden on Christian Street with individual plots, founded in 1976 and protected as a park in 1983. Members tend their own plots and share the orchard, the pollinator garden and the compost bins.
records.what_you_do: Members tend their own plot, attend five garden meetings and take part in five workdays each year, and help look after shared areas such as the orchard and compost.

schedule.text: Members attend five garden meetings and five workdays each year. The site does not list open hours.

cost.text: Members pay annual dues of $50, as the site's FAQ lists them.

first_step.how: Email swqvgarden@gmail.com to ask when the waitlist reopens, since it is closed now.
first_step.basis: The waitlist is closed, the wait to become a member is five to eight years, and only people who live inside the garden's catchment area can join.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site lists no open days or hours for visitors, and the waitlist is closed. Members tend their own plots and help with the shared orchard, pollinator garden and compost.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the garden was preserved in 1993; the garden's own history page says it became a protected park in 1983, so the summary uses 1983. Audience changed from public to residents because membership requires living inside the catchment (between the Delaware River and 6th Street, from Lombard Street to Washington Avenue). The member portal returned HTTP 403. The waitlist is closed and the page quotes a five to eight year wait, which is why the rating is 1. Dues are as the FAQ lists them.

records.name: Spanish American Professional Firefighters and EMS Association
records.summary: A Philadelphia association for firefighters and EMS workers that promotes Hispanic and Latino representation in emergency services. It also gives out free smoke detectors, teaches CPR and first aid, and hosts family events for neighbors.
records.what_you_do: Neighbors can take part in smoke detector giveaways, CPR and first aid classes, and family events. Fire and EMS personnel can join through the membership sign-up page, and friends and supporters can join as honorary members.

schedule.text: Smoke detector giveaways, CPR and first aid classes, and drives and cultural events run through the year. The outreach page gives no dates or places for them, and one-time events are listed separately on the events page.

cost.text: Smoke detectors are free. Honorary membership for friends and supporters lists no dues. Some events sell tickets, and the site does not list prices for CPR classes.

first_step.how: Join the email list on sapfa911.org to hear about the next smoke detector day, CPR class or family event.
first_step.basis: Programs are open to neighbors, and the site has a clear email sign-up and a public volunteer form, but the outreach page gives no dates or sign-up steps for classes.
first_step.what_to_expect: Smoke detector days give out free detectors along with fire-safety education. CPR and first aid classes are hands-on and taught by association members, and the site does not give their length or cost.

records.notes: The sapfa911.org contact page lists a Bronx, NY P.O. box and sapfa.org email addresses that do not match the Philadelphia group, and the about page places the association at 7100 Tulip Street. Those addresses are not recorded here; please confirm which contact the owner wants shown. The homepage states an establishment year of 1985. The dated events on the homepage (a Halloween party, a Thanksgiving food drive and a La Navidad party, all 2026) are kept out of the schedule and cost text on purpose.

records.name: SPEC Concerts
records.summary: The SPEC committee that books and runs Penn's annual Spring Fling concert each April. Members plan the show, work on marketing and event details, and help with the concert.
records.what_you_do: Students join the Concerts Committee through its listserv or general meetings. The April concert is for Penn students and community members, so people outside Penn can attend.

schedule.text: The committee holds general meetings through the school year, and the Spring Fling concert is held each April. The site does not list meeting times or places.

locations.label: SPEC office (200 Houston Hall)
locations.address: 200 Houston Hall, 3417 Spruce Street, Philadelphia, PA 19104

first_step.how: Email concerts@specevents.net to ask about the next general meeting, or join the committee's listserv if you are a Penn student.
first_step.basis: The committees take no application and students can join at any point in the semester, but the site does not say newcomers are specially welcomed and gives no meeting times.
first_step.what_to_expect: General meetings are held weekly during the year, where the committee talks about event ideas, listens to music and socializes. Members also get perks such as free entry to the April concert and a chance to meet artists backstage.

records.notes: The SPEC site describes eligibility three ways: students of all years at Penn (get-involved page), any undergraduate (about page) and students in general (committees page). The record follows tier 1 and says Penn students, and the committee should confirm. The concert attendance figures differ between pages, so none is recorded. The general SPEC address on the contact page is exec@specevents.net.

records.name: Springboard Meditation Sangha
records.summary: A meditation community rooted in Buddhist practice, open to anyone who wants to practice together. It offers free online sessions and in-person gatherings in Philadelphia and nearby.
records.what_you_do: Join a free online sit or discussion on the group's schedule, or attend an in-person gathering, such as a morning session or a residential retreat.

schedule.text: Regular online sessions run on Sundays (7 am, 8 am and 7 pm), Tuesdays (8 am, noon and 7 pm), Thursdays (8 am) and Fridays (11 am), with a monthly Zoom book group on second Fridays. Select Sunday mornings are in person at the Unitarian Society of Germantown.

locations.label: Unitarian Society of Germantown, Sullivan Chapel (in-person gatherings)

cost.text: Online sessions are free and open to the public. The site lists no fee for in-person gatherings and links to a donation page with no amounts.

first_step.how: Join a free online session through the Zoom link on the group's schedule page, or email info@springboardsangha.org about the beginner orientation class.
first_step.basis: A beginner orientation class exists (it runs once five people register), and the free online sessions are open to the public.
first_step.what_to_expect: The online schedule lists meditation sits and discussion or study groups, all free and open to the public. The pages we read do not say how long each session runs, so check the schedule page before you join.
first_visit_tips: Ask by email about the beginner orientation class before you come, since it runs only when enough people sign up.
For an in-person gathering, email first: the listings give dates and places but not parking, access or what to bring.

records.notes: The descriptions page lists nine regular programs with days and times. Only the orientation class states a sign-up rule (five people). The embedded calendar on the schedule page could not be read as text, so the times come from the descriptions page. The group has no page labeled new here. The 2026 in-person list gives dates without years; the page title carries 2026. A personal mailing address (c/o the contact person) on the homepage is deliberately not recorded.
